touches.text: TICKET (Abstract class - not a device, but a first class object; abstract)

The abstract ticket owns what every kind shares: its birth (cast) and its three parts, each with one job: the plan (only what a builder builds from), the metadata and state (what gates and doors read and write as it moves), and the history (the append-only log). WHY: one job per part reduces confusion; a builder reads the plan and nothing else (Akien, 2026-10-29 and 2026-11-02).
Coding Ticket: what we usually mean.
Each workflow step declares what it needs.
The ticket owns its refusals: a gate refuses a crossing on the ticket's behalf (ruling 2026-08-10). The gates are CodeMother's (10.3.5).

chain: the grammar every chart stage speaks. Stays in tools/: CodeMother is its heaviest user, not its only one (base, tester, rehearsal, build_inspector, proof_coverage, aider_shim, skills/chart also import it) (Q#50, Akien 2026-10-29).
Entry gates exist only to kick back what doesn't meet the entry requirements. Nothing in them is about who writes what.
operator_inbox: builds the operator's to-do list from live state. → Operator's machine (8.2.7)
proof_coverage: joins a ticket's falsifier clauses to the proofs that cover them and the seals that ran green. → Tester
ticket_inspector: completeness checks over tickets at rest. → CodeMother

rehearsal: the cheapest model reads a ticket cold and tries to build it on paper, saying where it got stopped or what is missing. → CodeMother PURPOSE: training data, so graph trees learn to judge "buildable as written" without an LLM call. WHY: a simulation costs tokens; it earns them only by teaching a tree. It was never meant to catch every shortcoming of every ticket, and where it teaches nothing it costs more than the builder simply building and recording where it got stuck. (Akien 2026-11-02, measured that day: 1,721 rehearsal records, $888 recorded cost, no reader but the BUILDME gate.) So until a learner reads the records, a rehearsal is not a BUILDME requirement. The records stand as the learner's first corpus. The read's shape holds: it is handed the plan steps, the frame (intention, why, falsifier), and what exists and what does not, measured before the read. "Cold" means no conversation, history, chart or process, not blind to the disk. (Akien 2026-10-29.)

skills/ (cairnhelp, challenge, chart, commit, intent, sorted, ...): Claude Code skills. The deterministic parts move out of markdown into CC device verbs: a skill's OS-side work runs as a script, and CC's shim processes the result and injects it into the session. Why: every habit captured that way is one CC no longer spends inference on, so CC gets faster. Precedent: UU's first charting pass did the first 3 or 4 steps in deterministic Python with no LLM until after, which saved about 90% of tokens, measured in real use. (Q#56, Akien 2026-11-05)
